heroLead: What I've studied, and what I'm studying now.
heroBody: Applied machine learning and statistics, aimed at problems in healthcare, finance and climate risk.

areas.title: AI in Healthcare
areas.body: Clinical risk prediction and public health statistics.

areas.title: AI in Finance
areas.body: Credit access for people traditional scoring leaves out.

areas.title: Climate Risk
areas.body: Flood and coastal erosion forecasting from satellite data.

papers.title: Who vapes? Demographic predictors of e-cigarette use among U.S. youth
papers.body: Using 28K+ records from the CDC's 2022 National Youth Tobacco Survey, our five-person team tested which demographic factors predict youth e-cigarette use. I led the statistical testing and literature review. Age, sex and grade level came out as significant risk factors. We presented to 200+ attendees at AUCC PFx.

papers.title: Forecasting flood risk with LSTMs and 12 years of geospatial data
papers.where: Youth In AI Research Lab · Accra
papers.body: An LSTM classifier trained on weather, time-series and geospatial data reached 93% accuracy and beat Random Forest and XGBoost by 12% under cross-validation. Features came from 18 flood-risk indicators I extracted with Python and Google Earth Engine.

papers.title: Stroke risk: which clinical and lifestyle factors matter most
papers.body: EDA and feature importance on 4,908 patient records surfaced six key risk factors. A TensorFlow network handled class imbalance with SMOTE and class weighting, reached 94% accuracy, and was validated on ROC-AUC and F1. It now runs as a live app.

papers.title: Predicting shoreline retreat on vulnerable coastlines
papers.body: Coastal erosion is taking homes and livelihoods along low-lying coastlines. This project models shoreline position over time from Sentinel-2 and Landsat imagery, to give coastal communities early warning and give policymakers evidence on sand collection and coastal vegetation loss.

papers.title: Does the data's origin matter? Cassava disease classification
papers.body: A three-way factorial ablation comparing models trained on real African field data, Western data and LLM-generated synthetic data, to see what each source actually contributes.

papers.title: Pen versus keyboard in Ghanaian universities
papers.body: Ghanaian high schools run on handwritten notes and exams. Universities run on typing. Building on Mueller and Oppenheimer's encoding hypothesis, this proposal sets out four study designs to test whether that switch affects academic performance.
